versions.name: Emissions-fuel decoupling
versions.definition: CO2 per heat input deviates from the unit's own baseline
versions.how_detected: Comparison of measured CO2 emissions against the unit's baseline using hourly CEMS data and regression analysis
benign_explanations: Fuel switching during normal operation (e.g., natural gas to fuel oil) without changing heat input
Load profile changes causing variable heat input
Maintenance activities affecting sensor calibration or measurement
Thermal drift in sensors due to aging or environmental conditions
Correction factor adjustments during data quality flagging

versions.name: Flatlined or stuck values
versions.definition: CO2 readings remain constant over extended periods despite operational changes
versions.how_detected: Statistical detection of lack of variation: standard deviation below threshold, runs test for randomness, or sustained identical values over multiple hours
benign_explanations: Measurement system failure or sensor malfunction
Unit was offline or in shutdown mode
Corrective maintenance (e.g., sensor reset, cleaning)
Data logging interruption or system reboot
Use of substitute values from neighboring units or backup systems

versions.name: Emissions reported while unit was not operating
versions.definition: CO2 values appear in the dataset for hours when the unit's opTime indicates no operation
versions.how_detected: Cross-reference of CO2 measurements against operational timeline (opTime) derived from heat input and generator status, flagged when emissions appear without operation
benign_explanations: Off-hour testing, commissioning, or plant startup procedures
Data import from neighboring units or regional databases
Unit in standby or spinning reserve mode
System calibration activities with fuel input but no actual generation
Utility load balancing or economic dispatch situations where units are 'on' but not generating

versions.name: Abrupt unexplained step change
versions.definition: Sudden jump or drop in CO2 values without documented operational events
versions.how_detected: Time-series analysis detecting discontinuities using statistical process control methods or manual review of incident logs
benign_explanations: Fuel switching event (documented in shift logs or operational plan)
Sudden load increase from market dispatch signals
Generator startup or shutdown ramp-up with associated thermal effects
Sensor sensitivity change due to environmental factors (temperature, humidity)
Measurement system bias correction or recalibration

versions.name: Reporting gap (missing hours)
versions.definition: Missing hourly CO2 measurements in the dataset due to telemetry loss or data transmission issues
versions.how_detected: Gap detection algorithms based on sequence analysis of timestamps or expected reporting schedule
benign_explanations: Planned maintenance affecting telemetry infrastructure
Network outage or communication failure during a storm event
Data storage or backup system recovery
Scheduled meter reading cycles (e.g., hourly instead of 5-minute)

versions.name: Heavy reliance on substituted or calculated CO2 values
versions.definition: Dataset contains predominantly calculated or substituted CO2 values rather than measured ones
versions.how_detected: Analysis of value flags (measured vs. calculated vs. substitute) showing majority non-measured values
benign_explanations: Regulatory reporting requiring filling of missing values with estimates
Use of emission factors to compute CO2 from heat input and fuel composition
Data interpolation or regression imputation to fill gaps
Remote sensing or proxy measurements due to unavailable onsite monitors

versions.name: Cross-source mismatch
versions.definition: CO2 values from different monitoring systems (continuous, batch, lab) disagree significantly
versions.how_detected: Inter-method comparison and statistical tests (e.g., paired t-test) showing significant differences beyond measurement uncertainty
benign_explanations: Different measurement protocols or standards across systems
Temporal offset between data collection times
Changes in fuel composition or calorific value
System-specific correction factors not uniformly applied

versions.name: Explained operational event
versions.definition: CO2 behavior matches a documented outage, startup, or shutdown event
versions.how_detected: Correlation of emission patterns with recorded operational events (opTime = 0, startup/shutdown ramps, maintenance events)
benign_explanations: Planned unit outage (maintenance, repair)
Scheduled startup/shutdown during unit commissioning or test
System reset or calibration procedure
Planned operational mode change (e.g., unit cycling for grid balancing)
